steps.content: ...Oh, there's also Sumire... Including Thistle, over 70% of the members have been found, if I'm not mistaken...
As for Coquelic, there seem to be some promising developments in the new treatment plan...

steps.speaker: Terminal
steps.content: One new meeting request pending approval. Applicant: Sinner Thistle. Desired time of meeting: As soon as possible.
Seeing the name that just flashed through your mind, you smile and press "Approve."

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, are you sure you want to meet her here?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: There are so many important documents here. If she... the loss would be significant. Besides, there is your health to consider.
Christina has talked with her, and the record has been set straight.
I don't think there will be any problems. Let's play it by ear then.
Presently, the office door opens and Thistle walks in.
That was quick! You haven't been waiting to see me, have you? Please take a seat.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: I... I think I'll stand. I... I just have a question to ask you.
I see. Well, as long as you're comfortable.
There is a silence. You wait for Thistle to speak. She looks so out of her element; under Hecate's watchful eye, she doesn't seem to know where to put her hands.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: I, um... I, um, wanted to ask you...
Thistle opens her mouth, guilt writ large on her face, but after much hemming and hawing, she closes it again.
She's taking forever to get out whatever she's come to say. Hecate's body, unable to maintain the state of high vigilance, relaxes slightly.
You laugh, feeling at ease now. Thistle is no longer that dangerous girl harboring feelings of intense hostility toward you. It's only pride that's keeping her from opening up.
Ah, I think I have a pretty good idea of what you want to say. Hecate, could we give us a minute?
Don't worry. Everything is gonna be fine.
Hecate understands what you're trying to say. Somewhat reluctantly, she leaves in silence. In the doorway, she, almost childishly, casts a stern look at Thistle, as if to say, "I haven't forgotten."
That look seems to make Thistle even more uneasy. It is some time before she starts speaking, in a halting voice.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: ...W-Why didn't you tell me?
Tell you what?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: That you were feeble because you were bearing some of the Mentor's Mania with your shackles...

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: You should've told me. I feel like an ungrateful idiot.
If I had told you, would you have believed me?
She falls silent, a somewhat guilty look on her face. Clearly, both of you know the answer to that question.
She doesn't stay silent for long. With a determined expression on her face, she brings up your previous questions.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: The things you tried to get out of me before, do you, um, still want to know them?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Since it isn't you who've harmed the Mentor, I guess it's okay to share them with you. Assuming, of course, that you still think they are useful to you.
Of course. I really want to know.
Thistle starts telling you what happened to her after the turmoil in N.F. 113, up until Coquelic's attempt on your life at the Bureau; that's the missing piece of your puzzle.

It was by no means a comfortable existence. The Garden had collapsed overnight, and Thistle had to flee with her severely wounded Mentor. It was a time of scarcity for them. Thistle kept a low profile in the West District, going into hiding when necessary but never stopping searching for the other Garden members.

As she recounts these tribulations of her life, there is no hint of complaint in her voice. She is in control of her emotions, and it is only when she mentions her Mentor's sudden departure—as well as her Mentor's failing health, and the missing Garden members, does she sound sorrowful.
This is the story of the Garden, told from a completely new perspective.
I see. So on the day the MBCC went to bring Coquelic in for questioning, you weren't on the scene?
And you don't know the whereabouts of the Sinners she commanded to leave her that day, or how they are doing now?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Yes. S-Sorry, I wish I could be more useful...
Nonsense. You've been a great help. Don't worry, we'll find your companions, every one of them.
Of course, we'll need your continued support. The Bureau knows very little about them, so we could use all the clues we can get regarding their whereabouts.
The same goes for Coquelic's treatment. We'll do our best to save her, but at the same time, we hope you and the other Garden members can offer whatever help you're able to provide.
Let's work together, Thistle.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Certainly. If the others are here too... I have no doubt the Mentor will get better. And things won't be like they used to be...

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Please let me know if there's anything I can do. Even though the Mentor always finds me annoying... I think there must be something I can do.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Anything I can do to help the Mentor, I mean anything, I'll do it.

She says these words with an intensity that makes you believe that if you were to say a certain panacea could be found in a certain place, she would dash out of the room to bring it back to save her beloved Mentor.

Actually, you find this intense side of her quite charming. She is genuine, proactive, and has unshakable core beliefs. If you look past her indifferent facade, she is very much like Christina. Yes, she can be impulsive, but at the same time, it can be invigorating to be around someone like her.

options: There is something you can do now.

choices.text: There is something you can do now.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: What is that?
Go see your Mentor.
You withdraw a document from the pile of papers near at hand, turn it, and hand it to her. It details the changes in Coquelic's vital signs following visits from Garden Sinners.
Since visits were allowed, many Garden Sinners have applied to visit Coquelic, and her vital signs have shown some improvement.
Although the medical staff were initially skeptical of my theory, she indeed responds to your voices.
Currently, a new treatment plan based on this phenomenon is in its final stages of validation. Maybe your visit could further bolster their confidence.
You thought Thistle would agree there and then, but she doesn't. Then you realize that she has never applied to visit Coquelic, which is unusual.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Me visiting my Mentor? Would it really help? I... I think that might not be a good idea.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: I... I'm so weak, I always mess up the Mentor's plans. She even finds my presence annoying...

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: If my visit ended up having the opposite effect... It's better to just let the other members visit her...
She finds you annoying because you're weak? Why would you think that?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: The Mentor told me so herself... on the morning of that day when you attacked.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: That day, I figured that since the Mentor hadn't had a petal bath in a while, I should prepare one for her. But when I tried to... she told me to leave, to get out of her sight. I still remember her words.

steps.speaker: Coquelic
steps.content: Ah, stop buzzing around in front of me. It's irritating! So much fuss! Could you please give me a moment's peace?

steps.speaker: Coquelic
steps.content: If you really have nothing better to do, then get out of my sight and send someone capable in. Garofano or Sumire, either would do.

Thistle's impression of Coquelic fails to capture the essence of the latter's demeanor, but judging by the fact that she could recite Coquelic's exact words, it's clear that she has taken her Mentor's disdain to heart.
Hmm, I don't know what a "capable" person is like in your Mentor's eyes, but I don't think you're weak.
You broke through the Bureau's security, made it all the way to my sickbed, and nearly finished me off.
And you say you're weak? Nightingale, who spent three days tabulating the damage you caused, would be among the first to disagree with you.
Your attempt at humor fails to dispel Thistle's gloom completely. She is still puzzled, but not as convinced of her Mentor's dislike of her as before.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: But if I'm not weak, then why would the Mentor...
I think it's because she wanted to get you out of harm's way.
A Sinner from the Garden told me that she seemed to be waiting for someone that day.
She must have known in advance about the MBCC's operation... So she made up some excuse and sent you away.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: The Mentor was prepared to fight you guys to the death, right?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: The only reason she sent me away at a time like that... could only be that she thought I was too weak to be of any help, right? She let the other members stay, after all.
For the first time, Thistle has laid bare her inner conflict for you to see. Looking at this perplexed girl, you make a valiant attempt not to smile.
Try looking at it from a different angle. As you know, that day in the Garden, your Mentor made herself the target of MBCC fire and ordered the other members to escape.
If you hadn't been sent away, would you have obeyed your Mentor's order and run away like the others?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Of course not!
She answers your question without the slightest hesitation, as if it were a reflex action. You can't help but laugh a little.
There you have it. If I were your Mentor, I'd have done the same thing.
It's not that she didn't trust you, and certainly not that she thought you were too weak and would hold her back.
It's because she knew, to protect you, she had to take a different approach with you than with the other members. There was no other way around it.
Her eyes light up at your words. You can't help but reach out and ruffle her hair, the way you do with Hella and Hecate.
Honestly, I didn't understand Coquelic at first. To me, she was just like a madwoman.
But now, having had the chance to meet you, I finally understand her. I've been there myself. I understand what one must do to protect, not just some of, but all of the people one cares about.
Everyone is unique. You take each person's personality into account when you try to devise a course of action to ensure their safety. What works with one person might not work with the next.
That's why you might choose to take someone under your wing to keep them safe, or you might decide to send them away to prevent harm from coming their way.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Sob... Mentor...

steps.speaker: Coquelic
steps.content: All right, stop crying now. Did you really think anybody could hurt me? Look at me, not a scratch—good as new. It was not a big deal. I told you I'd be back. Have I ever lied to you?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, you... Didn't you say you knew you hadn't fully recovered and wouldn't provoke her?
All right, all right... I'm totally fine. You can see it for yourself. Don't be mad now. I promise I won't do it again...
Something you said must have touched Thistle. She's now looking at you spellbound.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Mentor...
Hmm...

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: I mean, is that really what the Mentor thought?
Hmm...
As you ponder, the terminal makes a beep that signals the arrival of an urgent message.
Under Thistle's anxious gaze, you call up the message and read it.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Is... is it about the Mentor?
Yes.

Thistle correctly intuits the message is about Coquelic; it is as if they are connected spiritually in some way. This reminds you of how Coquelic, even in her deep slumber, is responding to the voices of the Garden members.
The message is from the medical team, saying that for the first time, Coquelic's vital signs have significantly improved, and there are no signs of relapse.
Go see her. Call her name, say whatever you want to say to her, ask whatever you want to ask her...
Maybe she'll wake up and answer you right away.
No sooner have you finished speaking than Thistle turns on her heel and runs away. Watching her retreating figure, you smile and shake your head, and then you push yourself up from the table.
Everyone is doing what they can to wake you up from your long sleep. I can't be lazy either. Of course, neither can you.
The Mentor of the Garden. I'm looking forward to the day you wake up. Hope it won't be far away. A lot of people are waiting for you to wake up.
